description: Public discussion and media coverage of hoax bomb threats against schools, airports and public buildings in Europe

messages.claim: The news media is driving panic over fake bomb threats purely for clicks and ad revenue; stop sharing the sensationalist coverage.

Sensational headlines about fake threats are just clickbait. Don't let the media scare you into giving them traffic.

Media hysteria around every single hoax needs to end. Refuse to engage with the sensationalism.

The hype machine is running full blast over empty threats. Block the fear-driven clickbait.

Stop retweeting alarmist coverage of these fake calls. The press is manufacturing terror for profit.
Unfollow outlets that push frantic breaking news alerts for every unverified hoax email.

We need to starve the press of attention when they blow harmless spam out of proportion.
Mainstream coverage of these hoaxes is pure fear porn. Do not engage, do not share.
Stop buying into the media circus. They make these prank threats sound ten times worse than they are.
The press won't stop hyping fake threats until we stop clicking their dramatic headlines.
Boycott sensationalist news reports about fake alerts. They profit off collective anxiety.
Stop feeding the news cycle's obsession with fake bomb scares. Clickbait journalism at its absolute worst.
News outlets are exploiting parents' worst fears for website traffic. Refuse to share their articles.
When the media covers every single prank email like a national emergency, society loses. Tune them out.
Stop letting panic merchants in the press dictate your mood. Ignore the sensationalist headlines.

messages.claim: Governments must introduce harsher legal penalties and mandatory prison time for anyone sending hoax threats.

If you shut down a school with a prank email, you belong behind bars. Laws need to be much harsher.

These pranksters waste police resources and terrorize kids. Throw the book at them with mandatory prison.
Tougher sentencing is the only way to deter these copy-paste bomb hoaxes. Stiff prison time now.
A small fine and community service won't stop hoaxers. We need long, mandatory prison sentences.
Legislators need to wake up and pass severe penalties for fake threats against schools and transit.
Demand harsher sentencing laws for anyone convicted of sending mass hoax threats.
Anyone who terrorizes public buildings with fake alerts deserves serious prison time, no parole.
We need strict statutory penalties for hoax threats. Slap on the wrist sentences must end.
Tougher laws now! If you send a fake threat to an airport or school, you should lose your freedom.
Make sending hoax threats a major felony with guaranteed jail time. It's the only real deterrent.
The legal system is far too soft on people calling in false alarms. Time to demand mandatory jail terms.
European parliaments must unite on this: harsh prison time for anyone orchestrating mass hoaxes.

Zero mercy for people sending fake bomb emails. Pass laws that lock them up for a decade.
We won't deter these disruptions until the legal consequences are genuinely terrifying. Stiff prison now.
Time to upgrade false bomb threats to severe criminal offenses with non-negotiable prison time.
If you clear out an airport with a fake call, you should pay for the costs and sit in a cell for years.
Soft-on-crime approaches to digital hoaxes are failing. Push for maximum prison sentences.
Governments need to show no leniency. Send a clear message with heavy prison sentences for hoaxers.
Demand an overhaul of the penal code to punish false alarms with serious, mandatory jail terms.
We need real consequences for shutting down public spaces. Strict criminal penalties are required.

messages.claim: Schools and transit hubs must stop shutting down completely over unverified, copy-paste email threats.

Total shutdowns over copy-paste emails are completely unnecessary. We need measured, realistic safety procedures.
We cannot paralyze public transport every time a troll sends a junk email. It's completely unsustainable.

Public venues need to stop overreacting to low-effort email hoaxes. Normal life shouldn't grind to a halt.
Canceling flights and closing schools over an email sent to 500 addresses makes zero sense.
Stop letting generic email templates derail our daily lives. Institutions need to stop panicking.
Authorities need a better screening process instead of immediately emptying entire train stations for spam.
Society cannot function if every unvetted email triggers a full city lockdown. Time for common sense.
Mass evacuations over mass-mailed junk text are reckless. We need smarter, proportional protocols.
Stop closing classrooms over generic spam. Teach officials how to spot obvious mass-sent hoaxes.

Total evacuations should be a last resort, not an automatic reaction to an obvious spam chain.
We are letting trolls dictate public life. Stop shutting down facilities over copy-paste threats.
Institutions need to stop the knee-jerk shutdowns. Better verification must happen before clearing buildings.
Paralyzing public transit over generic email spam creates more chaos than the threat itself.
Stop calling for instant mass evacuations over obvious fake messages. Keep calm and carry on.
A spam email shouldn't paralyze an entire school district. Protocols need a major reality check.

Full evacuations over bulk-sent emails make no sense. We need to stop falling into this trap.
Institutions should assess credibility before dumping thousands of people onto the street.
Stop giving low-effort hoaxes total power to freeze our cities. Change the evacuation rules.

variations: Demand our governments invest in modern cyber-investigation tools to track down these threat senders.

First responders are carrying the burden of these nonstop fake calls. Back them up and stay patient.
The whole point of these fake alerts is to stress out public services. Keep your head high and stay united.
